LESSON: GRAMMAR 7.3.1 TENSE: PRESENT AND PAST PROGRESSIVE ASPECT

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Grammar 7.3.1 Tense: Present and Past progressive aspect
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar 7.3.1 Tense: Present and Past progressive aspect, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade four General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to show when something happened? 2. How do we tell if an action is or was happening?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognize signs of words and phrases related to the theme,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar 7.3.1 Tense: Present and Past progressive aspect in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify the present and past progressive forms of the verb in oral, signed and written texts for communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar 7.3.1 Tense: Present and Past progressive aspect in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use the present and past progressive aspect correctly in oral, signed and written contexts for self-expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar 7.3.1 Tense: Present and Past progressive aspect in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of the present and past continuous tense in communication. ● In pairs, learners are guided to watch a captioned video clip or observe a signed demonstration of vocabulary related to technology. ● In pairs, learners are guided to identify, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to technology. ● In groups, learners are guided to listen to a radio or observe a signed or a sign interpreted TV programme and identify the present and past progressive aspect. ● In pairs or groups, learners are guided to give examples of actions in the present and past progressive aspect. ● In pairs learners are guided to use a given list of verbs to form sentences in the present and past continuous tense collaboratively. ● In groups, learners are guided to watch a video and write examples of the present and past continuous tense in a notebook. ● In groups, learners are guided to role-play or simulate an event in which they use the present and past continuous forms. ● Individually, learner is guided to identify present and past continuous forms from a newspaper or magazine article. ● In groups, learners are guided to complete a sentence using words in their present and past progressive aspect. 1. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar 7.3.1 Tense: Present and Past progressive aspect together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: learner confidently uses present and past progressive aspect in sentences correctly.

● Learning to learn: learning independently as learner is able to identify present and past progressive aspect from newspaper and magazine articles.

● Digital literacy: interacting with digital technology as learners manipulate digital devices to watch a video,listen or observe signed programs

featuring tenses.

Values:
● Responsibility: self-drive is cultivated as the learner is able take up roles during role play and simulation activities with peers.

● Unity: cooperation as learner is able to work in groups to carry out class activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life skills: Effective communication is nurtured as learners complete a sentence using words in their present and past progressive aspect.

Link to other subjects:

The learner can connect the concept of past and present tense to the learning in Kiswahili.
